newsitem.title: FRANCE: CYCLING-ABDOUJAPAROV SAYS HE'S PUZZLED BY DOPING CHARGE.
newsitem.headline: CYCLING-ABDOUJAPAROV SAYS HE'S PUZZLED BY DOPING CHARGE.

text.p: Uzbekistan's Djamolidine Abdoujaparov, expelled from the Tour de France for doping, said on Saturday he did not understand how he happened to fail a dope test.
"I don't know what happened. In eight years as a professional, it never happened to me. I don't understand," the Uzbek sprinter said.

He added he was probably given a banned product by a member of his Lotto team to ease his pain after a crash in the first stage on Sunday. Abdoujaparov was tested on Tuesday and banned from the race when the results of the test were announced on Friday.
"Our doctors know the products and I trust them. This man had been looking after me for years," he said.
Organisers did not say what substances had been found in his urines but sources close to the Lotto team said two banned products were detected, one of which being clenbuterol.

Clenbuterol became famous at last summer's Atlanta Olympics when a number of Russian athletes were banned for taking it. It is said to help breathing and Abdoujaparov said he had breathing problems after his crash.
Sources added the second substance was unknown and could come from Russia.
Lotto team officials said no decision had been made about Abdoujaparov's future with the team.
On Friday, team director Jean-Luc Vandenbroucke said he had sacked the staff member who gave the 33-year-old rider a banned product.
